sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: This briefing concerns Bruges in Gironde, near Bordeaux, not the Belgian city. Its centre is managed mostly with blue zones. The town put the Abadie car park and part of avenue de Verdun under blue-zone rules from 8 September 2025, to make access to shops easier [0], and announced that the Terrefort car park would become a blue zone from 15 October 2025, like the Borges and Abadie car parks: free but limited to one hour with a disc, 8:00 to 12:30 and 14:00 to 19:00 except Sundays and public holidays, with Bordeaux Métropole as the contracting authority [1]. Since 1 January 2025 the Métropole's low-emission zone covers everything inside the ring road and bars only unclassified vehicles, about 3.7% of Gironde households according to the page [3]; unclassified vehicles may still use 11 named park-and-rides, including Gare de Bruges, and the page does not say whether the whole commune of Bruges lies inside the zone [4]. The mobility page lists tram lines D and E and six bus lines serving the town and a planned 1.8 km road, walking and cycling link between Le Tasta and the centre [2]. The city's page on phase 3 of the town-centre redevelopment sets out a plan to rework public spaces between the town hall and Parc Treulon while keeping the parking offer, with start dates given as 2027 in one place and 2026-2028 in another; it is a plan, not a decision on parking numbers [17].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: Most of what changes sits in the Métropole's park-and-ride and event offer. Under the Keolis concession awarded in July 2022 a dynamic sign in Bruges shows live free spaces at nearby park-and-rides, and the Métropole voted a short-stay two-to-five-day offer on 29 September 2023 [5]. TBM lists the Bruges Centre park-and-ride on avenue de Terrefort, with 58 spaces for season-ticket holders only [6]; Bruges is not among the 11 park-and-rides that sell the two-to-five-day tickets [9]. For events at Stade Atlantique, tram C stops directly at the stadium and the main car park P5 at the Parc des Expositions costs 15 euros on site on concert days, with a 3-euro 'Pass Stade' return ticket [11]. Le Bonbon reported that parking there has been charged 15 euros per car since a match in October 2025, that the Métropole decided in August 2025 to harmonise pricing for events above 25,000 spectators, and that about 3,000 vehicles were counted in P5 at the last match against a capacity of 7,500; the fare for the Pass Stade is also given as 3.40 euros on TBM's page [12][14]. Bordeaux Métropole reports 364 on-street charging places at 146 stations [15]; Bruges lists two car-sharing stations and two carpool areas [16].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The park-and-rides are run by Keolis through TBM: same-day parking is included in a subscription, and others pay 4.50 euros for seven round trips for one to seven people [8]. TBM's pages disagree on the closing hours and on the fine for staying outside tram hours, 15 or 25 euros, so we state neither [7]. A February 2021 newsletter said the Bruges stops on tram C with most boardings were La Vache (770 per day) and Ausone (753), with Gare de Bruges at 456; these figures are about five years old [10].

Our data label six car parks as Bruges, with about 1,100 spaces, but the names indicate that some of them lie in neighbouring communes, such as Ravezies Le Bouscat, Hippodrome and the Gare de Blanquefort, so only Gare de Bruges (58 spaces) is certainly the one the town lists. Measured since 24 September 2026, the six together averaged about 38% on weekdays and 17% at weekends, weighted by spaces, a strong commuter pattern. Laharpe (80) averaged 74% on weekdays and reached full in a single Friday-morning reading, Liberation (137) 68%, Ravezies Le Bouscat (366) 37%, and Gare de Bruges only 13%. About four weeks of data.
